title: How the Python SDK builds provisioning key calls

prose.text: The Python provisioning key wrappers take a friendly key type and rebuild it into an association type in the URL. The Go list handling is in [[zpa.sdk-go.service-defects]], the API's association types are in [[zpa.api.provisioning-keys-wire]], and the product side is [[zpa.app-connectors.provisioning-keys]].

prose.label: Requests.

What an update returns is [[zpa.api.provisioning-keys-wire:update-returns-no-body]].

checks.do: Whether key_id and key_type were passed in the right order, since get, update and delete take key_id first while list and add take key_type first.
Whether the key type is one of the two this module maps, or one of the four the OAuth user-code module maps.
Whether a provisioning key update inside a microtenant actually carried the microtenant ID as a query parameter.
Whether a by-component lookup returned 404 because of the missing path slash.
Whether a Python update that changes the component passed it as zcomponent_id or zcomponentId, since component_id is sent as componentId.

key-types.statement: `simplify_key_type` maps `connector` to `CONNECTOR_GRP` and `service_edge` to `SERVICE_EDGE_GRP`, and every provisioning key URL is built from that value.

oauth-key-types.statement: The OAuth user-code module has its own `simplify_key_type` that also maps `assistant_group` to `NP_ASSISTANT_GRP` and `site_controller_group` to `SITE_CONTROLLER_GRP`.

key-type-raises.statement: A key type outside the mapped values raises `ValueError`, and `add_provisioning_key` and `update_provisioning_key` also raise `ValueError` when `key_type` is empty.

argument-order.statement: `list_provisioning_keys` and `add_provisioning_key` take `key_type` first; `get_provisioning_key`, `update_provisioning_key` and `delete_provisioning_key` take `key_id` first and `key_type` second.

quotes: def get_provisioning_key(self, key_id: str, key_type: str,
def update_provisioning_key(self, key_id: str, key_type: str,

update-params-in-headers.statement: `update_provisioning_key` calls `create_request(http_method, api_url, body, params, {})`, and `create_request` takes `headers` before `params`, so the microtenant dictionary is passed as headers and the params are empty.

quotes: body: dict = None, headers: dict = None, params: dict = None,
method: str, endpoint: str, body: dict = None, headers: dict = None, params: dict = None,

zcomponent-route.statement: `get_provisioning_key_by_zcomponent` builds `/associationType/{simplify_key_type(key_type)}zcomponent/{zcomponent_id}/provisioningKey`, with no slash between the association type and `zcomponent`.

python-create-body.statement: add_provisioning_key sends a body of name, maxUsage, enrollmentCertId and zcomponentId, taking the last two from the enrollment_cert_id and component_id arguments, and treats enrollment_cert_id as a plain optional argument for both key types.

quotes: key_type (str): The type of provisioning key, accepted values are: ``connector`` and ``service_edge``.
enrollment_cert_id (str): The unique id of the enrollment certificate for this provisioning key.
if not key_type: raise ValueError("key_type must be provided.")

python-add-key-leaks-snake-case.statement: The Python add_provisioning_key reads component_id and enrollment_cert_id with body.get rather than pop, so those snake_case keys stay in the body next to the camelCase keys it adds. The executor then camel-cases the body: enrollment_cert_id becomes the same enrollmentCertId key with the same value, and component_id becomes an extra componentId member next to zcomponentId.

evidence.after: # Preserve existing logic for other services

python-add-key-leaks-snake-case.conditions: Whether the server ignores the extra componentId member is not shown. Corrected because the snake_case keys do not reach the wire as such; previously "The Python add_provisioning_key reads component_id and enrollment_cert_id with body.get rather than pop, so those snake_case keys stay in the body next to the camelCase keys that are added."

python-update-key-needs-wire-keys.statement: The Python update_provisioning_key sends its keyword arguments as the body without remapping any key, and the executor camel-cases them: max_usage and enrollment_cert_id arrive as maxUsage and enrollmentCertId, but component_id arrives as componentId, not the zcomponentId that add_provisioning_key sends and the update docstring says it is mapped to.

quotes: component_id (str, optional): The component ID to associate (mapped to zcomponentId).

evidence.after: # Preserve existing logic for other services

python-update-key-needs-wire-keys.conditions: That no code in the function maps component_id rests on reading it. Corrected because the executor camel-cases the body (zpa.sdk-python.microtenant-scoping:body-camel), so only component_id is affected; previously "The Python update_provisioning_key sends its keyword arguments as the body with no key remapping, so a caller must supply the wire-cased keys, unlike add_provisioning_key, which accepts snake_case arguments."

update-query-microtenant.statement: On a provisioning key update the `microtenantId` query parameter is the client's configured microtenant, or absent, never the call's `microtenant_id`: the params passed are empty, and `create_request` builds the query parameters before it camel-cases the body, so the executor's lookup finds no `microtenantId` key in the body and falls back to the configuration.

update-query-microtenant.conditions: Read from the code for a caller who passes the snake_case microtenant_id keyword; not run against a tenant.

update-header-microtenant.title: Whether a microtenant ID sent as a header and in the body is honored on provisioning key update
update-header-microtenant.detail: update_provisioning_key passes the microtenant dictionary as request headers, and the microtenant ID also stays in the JSON body as microtenantId; the microtenantId query parameter carries only the client's configured microtenant (claim update-query-microtenant). Whether the service applies the header or the body field is not shown by the SDK or the OpenAPI document.
update-header-microtenant.blocks: trusting that a Python provisioning key update inside a microtenant reaches that microtenant

zcomponent-route-slash.summary: The Python and Go by-component provisioning key routes differ by a slash.

positions.says: Python joins the association type and `zcomponent` with no slash.
Go separates them with a slash.

zcomponent-route-slash.impact: The Python by-component method requests a path that the Go package does not use; which one the service accepts is not shown.
